name: Korvain Dynamics Blast Visor
description:
A flip-up ballistic visor mounted on a lightweight titanium headframe, rated for fragmentation and low-velocity projectile deflection. The visor itself is layered polycarbonate with an anti-spall coating on the interior. When raised, it locks above the forehead; when lowered, it covers the face from hairline to chin.

Used by breaching teams, demolitions crews, and the kind of private security that expects to be shot at. The Blast Visor does not pretend to be subtle — its presence communicates that the wearer is prepared for violence.
functionality: Fragmentation protection, low-velocity projectile deflection, flip-up mechanism
what_it_says: You expect things to explode near your face and you've budgeted accordingly.
story_hooks: A Blast Visor recovered from a failed bank heist has a name etched on the interior — belonging to a corponation security consultant who was supposedly on shift that night.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist headpiece that commands attention—angular titanium frame with a prominent flip-up visor assembly. When lowered, it presents a fortress-like appearance; when raised, the visor locks horizontally above the forehead like a deployed shield. The aesthetic is pure function: industrial, aggressive, unapologetically tactical.
physical_description.fit: Snug, secure fit against the skull and upper face. The titanium frame distributes weight evenly across the crown and temples. The visor mechanism allows for rapid deployment without shifting. Designed for stability during high-impact scenarios.
physical_description.primary_material: Lightweight titanium alloy frame (aerospace-grade), layered polycarbonate visor with anti-spall ceramic interior coating
physical_description.texture: Smooth, cold metal surfaces on the frame with fine milling marks. The polycarbonate visor has a subtle frosted quality from the anti-spall treatment; faint stress marks may appear from impact absorption tests.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray titanium with jet-black polycarbonate visor. Narrow accent line in industrial orange (Korvain Dynamics branding) along the frame's lateral edge. Minimal ornamentation.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic locking mechanism for visor deployment; friction-fit headband with tension adjustment via recessed titanium screws at the rear
distinctive_features: Flip-up polycarbonate visor with ballistic rating stamps etched into the frame
Anti-spall interior coating visible as matte black underside
Korvain Dynamics logo embossed on right temple
Integrated ventilation slots to prevent fogging
Quick-release mounting points for helmet cams or targeting assists
Reinforced nose guard extending down the centerline
Scratches and minor stress fractures typical of field use
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 hybrid. High-end military/security contractor equipment. Expensive enough to signal serious training and dangerous work, accessible to well-funded private teams rather than exclusive to Tier 1 corpo elite.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by breaching specialists, demolitions crews, armed corporate security, and mercenaries. Its presence signals 'I expect gunfire.' Street gangs and Tier 5 operators might scavenge or counterfeit versions, but authentic Korvain gear carries weight in professional combat circles.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn, with cosmetic scuffs on the frame, possible spall marks or minor cracks in the visor from deflected rounds. May show stress patterns from repeated deployment cycles. Rarely pristine unless freshly issued.
